title: Animation
summary: A reference object pointing to an animation asset by AnimationId. You don't play it directly — Animator:LoadAnimation turns it into an AnimationTrack you control.

properties.name: AnimationId
properties.description: The asset: "rbxassetid://507770239". Must be owned/usable by your experience.

explanation.whatItIs: The 'cassette tape' of animation: an Instance that names which animation to load. Playback lives on AnimationTrack.
explanation.whyItExists: Animations are assets; Roblox needs an Instance to reference and configure them (and to place in StarterPlayer defaults).
whenToUse: Creating Animation instances to load via Animator
Configuring default animations (the Animate script uses these)
Emotes and ability animations stored as assets
whenNotToUse: Expecting to Play() an Animation — that's AnimationTrack
Non-character animation — tween parts or use Motor6D transforms instead
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
Animation (the asset pointer)
      │ Animator:LoadAnimation(animation)
      ▼
AnimationTrack (the player)
      │ :Play(), :Stop(), .Stopped
      ▼
Motor6D transforms animate → character moves
```
tips: Upload animations via the Animation Editor; note the asset id
Ownership rules: animations must be created/owned by the experience or its creator
commonMistakes: Loading an animation whose asset isn't usable in your experience → load error

examples.title: From asset to playing track
examples.code:
local animation = Instance.new("Animation")
animation.AnimationId = "rbxassetid://507770239"

local animator = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid"):WaitForChild("Animator")
local track = animator:LoadAnimation(animation)
track.Looped = false
track:Play()

track.Stopped:Connect(function()
    print("Animation finished")
end)
